title: Astrid and the Witness
premise: Lior Nakamura, a night-shift dispatcher who treats every fare like a puzzle to be closed, is stunned when a murdered stranger is found wearing clothes stolen from their own closet — and the only witness, a mute elderly woman named Astrid Voss, keeps appearing on Lior's dispatch log at addresses that shouldn't exist. As the trial of the accused killer approaches, Lior discovers that Astrid's late husband kept a ledger disguised as taxi route cards, documenting decades of payoffs that protected a powerful family. Working outside the law because the evidence would never survive a corrupt courtroom, Lior decodes the ledger with Astrid's help, exposes the true killer — the victim's own business partner — and finally understands that belonging means choosing your people, not inheriting them.
about_author: Gideon Dunmore is the pen name of a former municipal court clerk who spent eleven years watching justice bend around money before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about ordinary people who refuse to wait for permission to do what's right.

chapters.title: The Last Fare
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. On an unremarkable night shift, Lior dispatches a cab to a passenger who never arrives; hours later, police call: a body found in a ravine, dressed in Lior's own missing jacket and scarf. The emotional beat is cold shock — the dispatcher's ordered world cracking open as they become a suspect's curiosity rather than its solver.

chapters.title: Astrid in the Logbook
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Reviewing dispatch records under police pressure, Lior finds the victim called three times from the home of Astrid Voss, a silent old woman Lior has driven past for years but never met. Detective Reyes warns Lior off. Beat: uneasy fascination — the first thread pulled from a knot that won't hold.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior visits Astrid's sagging Victorian and communicates through notes and gestures; Astrid presses a taxi route card into their hand — one of hundreds her late husband Emil collected. Beat: tentative connection across silence, and the first hint that Emil left something deliberate behind.

chapters.title: Clothes That Fit a Stranger
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Forensics confirms the clothing was taken during a break-in at Lior's building — someone wanted the body mistaken for Lior. Reyes admits the frame-up theory quietly, off the record. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve; Lior realizes they weren't random collateral, they were a target.

chapters.title: Route Cards
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior/Astrid POV (Astrid's sections rendered as italicized memory). Astrid recalls Emil sorting route cards by color every Sunday; Lior notices the cards' fares don't match any real trips. Beat: dawning wonder — the ledger hidden in plain sight begins to surface.

chapters.title: The Trial Date
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The accused, dockworker Tomas Rehn, pleads innocent; his court-appointed lawyer is visibly outmatched by the city's star prosecutor, Adrian Kessler, whose family name appears oddly often in Emil's route cards. Beat: dread — the clock starts ticking toward a verdict built on lies.

chapters.title: What the Colors Mean
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Lior maps card colors against dates and discovers green cards cluster around payments from the Kessler shipping fortune; Astrid's memories reveal Emil was a driver who saw too much and started keeping receipts. Beat: purpose ignites — a hobby becomes a mission.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching the House
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A gray sedan idles outside Astrid's street; her porch light shatters that night. Lior moves her temporarily to a motel under a false booking name through the cab company. Beat: protectiveness hardening into stakes — this is no longer just Lior's mystery.

chapters.title: Tomas Talks
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior visits Tomas in holding and finds a frightened man who says he drove the victim once and was paid to forget it — by someone whose face he'll only describe as 'the prosecutor's shadow.' Beat: moral vertigo; the legal system itself looks complicit.

chapters.title: Emil's Last Run
chapters.summary: Astrid POV. In memory, Emil's final night: a green-card pickup at the Kessler warehouse, a threat delivered gently, and his decision to hide the master sequence inside the one thing no one would steal — a dead man's taxi memorabilia. Beat: grief transmuted into inheritance.

chapters.title: The Sequence
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Cross-referencing card numbers with old garage shift sheets, Lior cracks the ordering principle: the ledger reads as a route through time, each 'fare' a payment, each tip percentage a code for the amount. Beat: triumph cut short — the decoded pages name a current payoff, dated last month.

chapters.title: Kessler's Offer
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Adrian Kessler corners Lior at a courthouse café, offering a 'consulting retainer' and implying Astrid's care costs could be handled generously. Beat: cold fury — corruption doesn't threaten first, it buys first, and Lior refuses in a way Kessler will remember.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior loses dispatch shifts, their landlord gets an anonymous complaint, and Reyes warns them off officially. The cab company owner, Marisol, quietly backs Lior anyway. Beat: isolation answered by chosen loyalty — belonging defined against pressure.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Couldn't Speak
chapters.summary: Astrid POV. Present-day: Astrid, frustrated by silence, writes her fullest statement yet — she saw the victim alive the night he died, leaving the Kessler warehouse with a briefcase. Beat: reclamation of voice; the witness becomes testimony.

chapters.title: The Briefcase Route
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Following the ledger's final entries, Lior traces the payoff chain to a storage unit holding the briefcase's twin — and photos proving the victim was blackmailing Kessler's partner-in-payments, shipping magnate Dale Voss, Astrid's estranged nephew. Beat: devastating twist — the inheritance theme turns literal and cruel.

chapters.title: Family Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid POV. Astrid confronts the truth: Dale knew Emil's ledger existed all along and let Astrid live as bait, assuming she'd never decode it. She sends Lior one word: RUN. Beat: betrayal inside bloodline, courage inside frailty.

chapters.title: Ravine Road
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Summoned by a fake dispatch call, Lior is ambushed at the original crime scene; they escape using a cab company trick — killing their phone signal and flagging a passing night driver. Beat: survival by craft; the dispatcher becomes their own best fare.

chapters.title: Everything in Evidence
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. With trial two days away, Lior copies the decoded ledger and delivers sets to Reyes, a journalist, and the defense lawyer simultaneously — justice outside the law by making it impossible to bury. Beat: strategic sacrifice; Lior gives up control to guarantee truth survives.

chapters.title: The Verdict Room
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, courtroom climax. Kessler's case collapses as the defense introduces the ledger; Dale Voss, panicking on the stand, implicates Kessler's office in the payoffs and the murder cover-up. Tomas walks free. Beat: catharsis — the system bends, but only because outsiders forced it straight.

chapters.title: What Dale Buried
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Arrested for the murder, Dale confesses: the victim died when the blackmail handoff turned violent, and framing Lior was meant to muddy the water. Astrid attends the arraignment and does not look away. Beat: grim satisfaction — accountability without comfort.

chapters.title: Astrid Speaks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At Emil's reopened grave-side gathering, Astrid speaks aloud for the first time in years — a single sentence thanking the stranger who became family. Lior formally takes over managing her affairs, and Marisol offers them both a place in the company's future. Beat: warmth after ruin; belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Night Shift, New Routes
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Months later, Lior dispatches the night shift from a desk beside a framed green route card, closing cases the way they always have — one fare, one truth at a time. A new mysterious call comes in; Lior smiles and picks up. Beat: quiet renewal — the loop closes, the watcher remains.
